findings.title: Backup code single-use is not enforced atomically
findings.body: The backup code is consumed by reading the encrypted list, setting the matched entry to null in memory, and writing the whole list back with a plain update. Nothing ties the write to the value that was read. Two concurrent login requests that present the same valid code (both pass the password check and read the same list) will both succeed, and the second write will simply overwrite the first. A code documented as 'can be used exactly once' can therefore be redeemed more than once. A conditional update (compare-and-swap on the stored ciphertext, or a transaction with a re-check) is needed.

findings.title: missing_backup_codes message points to a settings option that does not exist
findings.body: The message tells users 'No backup codes found. Please generate them in your settings.' No regenerate or view-codes UI is added by this PR. Codes are only created during the initial 2FA setup, and disabling 2FA is required to get new ones. Users who see this message are sent to a place where they cannot act on it, so the text is misleading.

findings.title: Backup codes are unrecoverable if the dialog is dismissed without clicking Close
findings.body: Backup codes are shown only in the DisplayBackupCodes step, and the dialog's own close control (onOpenChange / Escape / overlay click) bypasses the 'backup-codes-close' button. The codes are stored hashed-to-nothing (encrypted only, and never shown again). Once the user dismisses the dialog, the codes can no longer be retrieved, and the only way to get new ones is to disable and re-enable 2FA. Nothing in the flow forces the user to acknowledge or save the codes before dismissal.

findings.title: Copy button reports success even if the clipboard write fails
findings.body: navigator.clipboard.writeText(...) is not awaited or caught, and the success toast is shown unconditionally. The Clipboard API rejects in insecure contexts or when permission is denied, so the user gets a 'Backup codes copied!' toast while nothing was copied, and an unhandled promise rejection is produced.

findings.title: Interactive Button rendered inside an anchor element
findings.body: The download control nests a <Button> (a <button> element) inside an <a download> element. Interactive content inside <a> is invalid HTML, has inconsistent keyboard and click behaviour across browsers, and is an accessibility problem. The anchor should carry the styling or the button should be the link.

findings.title: Password visibility toggle removed from keyboard tab order for all PasswordField uses
findings.body: tabIndex={-1} is added to the show/hide password button inside the shared PasswordField component. This affects every password field in the app, not only the 2FA flow, and makes the toggle unreachable by keyboard users. The change is unrelated to backup codes and is an accessibility regression.

findings.title: Non-string backupCode in request body causes an unhandled exception
findings.body: req.body.backupCode.replaceAll(...) assumes a string. A client sending a number, object, or array as backupCode (the body is unvalidated JSON) throws a TypeError, which surfaces as a 500 rather than a 400 IncorrectBackupCode. The same pattern exists in next-auth-options.ts for credentials.backupCode.

findings.title: Backup-code login path has no test coverage
findings.body: The new login flow (Lost access, backup code submission, incorrect and missing backup code errors, and single-use consumption) is not exercised by any test. The only backup-code assertions are that the download, copy, and close buttons exist in the setup dialog. The PR description says the feature is untested, and the TODO only defers this. The core behaviour of the feature, including the single-use guarantee, is unverified.
